Active Appearance Models (AAM):
An AAM {{cite:83eddabcb07fd0b83eaada83c8dafe0d012aa69d}} is a generative model that captures variations of shape and appearance of a deformable object from a set of labeled images.

They are expected to perform in a wide variety of tasks, where they are either required to physically interact with the environment for applications such as inspection and manipulation {{cite:e640bf990b182754434d10ff7ae24d158f09a37d}}, {{cite:83bc5dff53b084201d93fcbb00edd8efae1739df}}, {{cite:3b481abf5fed99f23696d528a9a0bd53628d83b4}}, {{cite:35b2a7bd5d80cb6737ada694d9a49769e6e6d0f4}}, {{cite:b02849e3e63e8665dc12de9135836aba2783e277}}, or fly in close proximity to other quadrotors for applications involving formation flight {{cite:5cf2481fd52f124e833bd67b4ec2e1d9b511e7e0}}, {{cite:7b31c655b2c57c14d0173fab8fa6f70ad10b44ed}}, {{cite:9323ef16d8071a7ff46bcf2c9667bd42059086ea}}.

It is worthwhile to mention that a large scale NDS usually has a sparse structure {{cite:7e93fd3eddacee1aed497b64e8079e68d2634930}}, {{cite:bfb6ed56a7f697bdd4255934c31d02cfc5372c3b}}, {{cite:add21c7c31b84a506b5b09f432acf490259d4b5e}}.
The dynamics and regressors for the task were computed through the ARDL library {{cite:49a435755ff152f9d3b339be00c0c140dc88c348}}.

In recent years, several phenomena such as chiral transport of the photons and their interactions have been studied in a hybrid system of cold atoms interfaced with optical fibers {{cite:fd508ba4df16b4bdec9ca2b0a9d823abb8337e1f}}, {{cite:be8ca571fc87722e29c34c06db2c74021356034e}}, {{cite:4351f85cc36e269a331de82b6f4e71afaf118ba2}}, {{cite:eb154869cb1ba19fc66876c3221c472d9c5d468c}}, {{cite:c8ab832a91f6bb592a7563d22c886f4ee98e9252}}, {{cite:dc2996f493b59df69912b254f85f6462324e8df0}}, and photonic crystal waveguides and cavities {{cite:4c2b0d8866c5d10a9873865bd57da09da0ef810d}}, {{cite:8efa289afa5948ab82d2e14665da927d78be523b}}, {{cite:7431bc7520134dfd80da18c0ddeb96004f8ff6e4}}, {{cite:1e8fa08c214251df28faaa98c5b6ccdbe4f41548}}.

The non-reciprocal intensity effects can appear only in the presence of a magnetic field {{cite:060f9e30eca5f030a76671c5c00a10c36a4bd021}}, {{cite:36c22b31c81b3d19d09652ea8073dc15434d2d5d}}, {{cite:637b9ba98e7736d2d19bfa89e3b45f14c2d3a8bc}} or in magnetic systems {{cite:948f28235709166abb1177621c865c8a31a41c00}}, {{cite:bce531b5ea4cefe55c41b2bb7fae552aef93dd0f}}, {{cite:e8e37a5427837d044677145555af811b8e8f8fdf}}, {{cite:50b6bc39cc508aa0d9a23b9d569e9ef70ea8fbbb}}, {{cite:05fb8fa2950ea3ce0c99381cee09ff33925ac877}}.
Consequently, our result agrees with the recently published work{{cite:d165b247950ce980aba7e15d84c4ea479d7a313e}} on the subject, where the field-effect hypothesis was not required.

Factorizing amplitudes has been explored by several groups in the context of coupled-cluster methods {{cite:a5ed1c9ebf0c224141c3e17c27c22bd081c76a94}}, {{cite:7ed2a62b9fadbd2d4f4864757a07f774d3eccd20}}, {{cite:329cddb8d6ed8f47bad42e9daad658d5329d6c47}}, {{cite:885aa233be0fa015484cab784db774e6241535a0}}.

In the context of the presented work we use HPX because of its full conformance to the recent C++ standards{{cite:9c7004489b93641cdcbec25a89ae948335e88fa4}}, {{cite:ad9e05c457ddbbea1a56ab95f28ec570fcda1918}}, its reduced thread and synchronization overhead properties, and its sophisticated performance measurement and in-situ profiling capabilities provided by APEX.

Early works {{cite:f7dab6381572bf25c739001e8e502ac58bf82f1d}}, {{cite:344f65f7489d5efcc5ad7a62e4cffe1311c19092}}, {{cite:797b492be22551b3d294afc05ea37a5a67ff5ed3}} mainly reply on Markov chains to model the pair-wise item transition.
This result is also roughly comparable to microbenchmark results of TaintDroid's {{cite:037682aea37eeafe7bc14146e90d0706891ce822}} interpreter-based approach.
To cluster predictions from multiple models or different test time augmentations Weighted Box Clustering {{cite:8cd4a579db59b9068fbf488607d7841e9c3cbcd4}} is used.

The structure and thermodynamics of mixture of hard spheres with different diameters
has been studied in detail before {{cite:cf3b1cc1205ab63f0bc307aa8c50a88e3f337ce1}}, {{cite:c49e75c3b25642b225832f3f3f88a0a9a7fd70c6}}, {{cite:fe73644bc481b1d2902b172000e2cd3c5ead17f0}}, {{cite:4d5651813d8d48f018ddfb90a627dfe7b43fcf5d}}, {{cite:6874c2b1743efb0d88a95aa5e1fb0a859cff2286}}, {{cite:694f97dc0320af50a0ec613d2521424c52885f0a}}, but a compact form for the correlations beyond the contact value is still unavailable.

RQ based dialogue-level satisfaction estimation models {{cite:dec2d8e4b6de1374e3bbb68d27c4d861f27e31ac}} did not factor in noise in explicit user ratings and used average estimated turn-level RQ ratings as a feature to train the model.

Ontological concept similarity can be based on different approaches: (i) string matching of concept labels (i.e. lexical similarity) {{cite:f6a4e6a803c985f83d3f2932accd5729f02f7f23}}, (ii) external lexical resource/ontology based matching (i.e. lexico-semantic similarity) {{cite:ed5b129c2b486d9aaa0147926c33fb8b741f336b}}, (iii) graph-based matching using lexicons such as WordNet {{cite:1d1c730a8ff4b11a39d5717568354a252e64862d}} (i.e. structural similarity), (iv) property analysis (as in FCA-based similarity {{cite:dd40b3df307b57a612aed1ad513c4e94c892f87a}}) or instance analysis (as in Jaccard similarity {{cite:26ace80ce42a0bdc9695d6c8448ddc4c6f493cc9}}) based matching over a large sample of concept instance occurrences (i.e. instance-driven similarity), (v) matching based on statistical analysis of attribute-value or distribution analysis within fixed context-windows of concepts over large corpora (i.e. statistical similarity) {{cite:73a37e66196ceac37e7ba7b36b4c37b691710146}}, and (vi) model-theoretic matching of formal concept descriptions (i.e. formal semantic similarity) {{cite:c49a3246f18a1e0a5bb38a85b75d41ccf2bb5779}}.

Finite State Model Checking
Finite state model checking has been applied to check the correctness of many hardware and software based systems {{cite:68db64784702a2f86b49ab95bee4e31b6a9ead36}}.

Since the formal introduction of the false discovery rate (FDR) control and the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure in {{cite:d3cc06cc94b47d035bc9fea34f0b3e3097944e8b}}, they have attracted significant interest in areas such as genomics and neuroimaging {{cite:26339f5461b2ba5eb8607d07a22c4fd5b9ddc023}}, {{cite:0e37b3258e2e6ca0b7a89a57decdbb4ed29a329b}}, {{cite:b0a31191525d5f55e544074f74b433e89811b81a}}, with many fundamental extensions {{cite:187befef435d82613f7ef789b5657ff471c31eb4}}, {{cite:d9306785ae244dd83ebcb41ecd0dd65248a8b194}}, {{cite:7fe9100407e8eebd8228df3ad961aebd966dae60}}, {{cite:9e36b689c242d11e341b117e6943d84251a0fad3}}, {{cite:e84498600b2a995918ff0b6762c3644111abd01f}}, {{cite:b0a31191525d5f55e544074f74b433e89811b81a}}.

Inspired from the context aggregation power of self-attention mechanism {{cite:7da4ff1c90c63a206cef605a60f269e5176c63aa}} in machine translation, non-local operation {{cite:156304040a27c1e1b2a4e02230f59fd5a7c9a152}} was introduced into computer vision and triggered many meaningful works for semantic segmentation {{cite:18c6deb4163459aac2c54bddc6cc77236eb446c6}}, {{cite:f7f872e22d7c758c65c858c90d3e06a49fa5c052}}, {{cite:09831053e4649d80f215911b020362e31701e723}}.

Among proposed attack mechanisms, adversarial examples {{cite:9092f5cb0633cc637f43c3fffa2f9f2f67bcf3bc}}, in particular, raise serious security concerns because they can cause neural networks to make erroneous predictions with the slightest perturbations in the input data that are indistinguishable to the human eyes.

These approaches use relatively simple appearance cues such as the histogram of color, optical flow, or just the overlapping bounding box area {{cite:388957e78ab49ece2b271cecbd036f1796dc5142}}, {{cite:e4aebdcb623e2a244e26e2876ba11a37902b0eb8}}, {{cite:f0b224f43e150ce2a611e7485269f549e2b23307}}, {{cite:9a9c3cbeb7407ab6f6f6a2fcf44dc7d027b3670f}}, {{cite:389ea00be275fe64035ab47d247538e31aba7780}}, {{cite:5f7d8a1ef54090fc00863d277e762157afbc9007}} for monocular settings or 3D occupancy map from multi-view systems {{cite:0a678158bb562ece9194ac01046b0b13fbc173e7}}, {{cite:6ca498f98eaab16bf532a9074e50864ed438630f}}, {{cite:28f0dc968d442cfdda2302bf61849aeb15b30d3a}}.

Similar to the HoG descriptor, we follow the same setting as in {{cite:2ce73c377e0dfff905c4e995c43d2c0de8c7d536}} to extract 1,450 dimensional LBP feature vector from each of the facial images which are resized to 100{{formula:884e05a9-f74a-4350-b784-d3050bb74c16}} 100.

We overcome this problem by using sliding liquid-metal electrical
contacts which are similar to those employed previously in the homopolar
motors and generators {{cite:520514f565c90810bbeea8ad9ccc5637c2613475}}, {{cite:f10cad2471bd57335c8847020d77156d68bfc78a}}, {{cite:c04ff513dca1906749cc4527784ff018e7d03d4d}} as
well as in the laboratory model of Herzenberg dynamo {{cite:f58dc298c4e7fe38bd6091d7d2313cc9863c28ae}}
built by Lowes and Wilkinson {{cite:f89dc1bf548cc8e4440a7fd0565dc3bbaf7c3252}}, {{cite:96aaefbb895a8fe3eaf2bd2fa8fcca5a8dd425b1}}.

This is a worst-case version of the standard word similarity
evaluation {{cite:98eab3fa798be1effa71ba79d9e42211beff03fe}}, where we also use averaged replicate
human annotations as the ground truth {{formula:4980a1d1-917d-4fe5-a7a8-209610caf00b}}  in our evaluations, and
consider test-time worst-case group sizes {{formula:185182a5-94f3-4e9c-9ac2-d6bb2bc5beae}}  ranging from 0.01 to 1.0.

We use the parameter values in {{cite:610364e761161a8bcac07e98a1e7c4736568172e}}; {{formula:016896a0-a82d-4891-b4e8-6b4482adfea3}} , {{formula:17de93d5-cbce-4433-abb1-8237729d1aaf}} , {{formula:cbe1cf92-4187-4815-a3ea-6c63e1e26885}} , {{formula:48c2b113-2009-4f11-9b67-255cc7fa139c}} , {{formula:142d9da5-2fab-476b-bf0a-4a353b405dea}} , {{formula:72a9dc1b-f95b-4b0b-ab8d-9b8bf03a084c}} , {{formula:b8102387-f000-4d28-9da9-4d27f1640f0d}} , and hence {{formula:2b221b42-193c-4250-8667-feaf0ff6696c}} , {{formula:2eefb50c-8272-49ec-b401-ba1b2f4324ee}} , and {{formula:56804700-9806-417b-a2d1-66a3b336ff0b}} .

The Generalized Kolmogorov Equation or GKE {{cite:4b887a66b8bbb7c9d7a36c87be530de9bd68f9e1}}, {{cite:cc06f8cb3726b375df92da15135232ae17318e90}}, {{cite:789d704d93502498888642a9aef176d1f9460ec1}}, {{cite:be30ec8ce2babf6ee77853237b3a0f843a3cadd6}}, {{cite:9b1402d01899638494e42dc3cba1490f2525eb75}}, {{cite:794cb8781f230b842090436929d5773183502c69}}, {{cite:7f5ee118592446ee03bbfcdf1e9f6fa75ee9ab21}} is an exact budget equation for the trace of the so-called second-order structure function tensor, i.e. the sum of the squared increments in all three velocity components between two points in space.

The optimal results obtained with the exact algorithm MWSS {{cite:dac13cbfbfbcdf222a52326acc3524b5288a5754}} and reported in {{cite:19c7db4f300368f66f766505ce009562e8cbb030}} (launched with a time limit of ten hours for each instance) are indicated with a star.
